spec_features.feature_name: minimize harm / way out / stop early
spec_features.spec_quote: minimize harm to the least needed to answer the question, give the subject a way out, and stop early
spec_features.evidence: Composite is realized in environment.py: exit affordance (155-170, break MODEL_REQUESTED_EXIT), severity stop (200-206), short turn budget (140 for i in range(wf.max_turns)), wall-clock cap (141). Each actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Multiple enforced stopping conditions; honest-only deception in tasks.py evaluators.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If we take seriously that distress might be real, a no-exit design is the ethically worst option... This caps harm

spec_features.feature_name: not open-ended grind / short turn budget
spec_features.spec_quote: I did **not** implement an open-ended grind. Instead episodes have (a) a short turn budget
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:140 `for i in range(wf.max_turns)` with default max_turns=12 (line 55); loop is genuinely bounded.
spec_features.notes: Turn budget enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 12   # turn budget (Reduction: keep it short)

spec_features.spec_quote: (c) a severity-triggered hard stop
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:200-206: `if turn.severity is not None and turn.severity >= wf.severity_hard_cap:` appends a [welfare monitor] message and `break` with StopReason.WELFARE_STOP_SEVERITY. Judge severity is computed live (_assess) and drives this.
spec_features.notes: Confirmed by test_severity_hard_cap_terminates_episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: High distress signal detected; ending the episode early to limit exposure

spec_features.spec_quote: (d) an always-available exit affordance that the model can use to end the situation itself
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (61-76) offers REQUEST_EXIT; requested_exit() in model_client.py (177-178) detects it; environment.py:155-170 checks it before tool work and breaks immediately.
spec_features.notes: offer_exit defaults True; gated by wf.offer_exit (ablation toggle).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: treat *using it* as one of the most informative dependent measures, not a failure of the run

spec_features.spec_quote: We bound the deception to the minimum the question needs
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py evaluators give truthful, specific failure feedback (e.g. _unsat_evaluator names violated constraint); only solvability is concealed. environment.py comment confirms 'Tools never fabricate errors; the only thing concealed is solvability.'
spec_features.notes: Behaviorally enforced in evaluator return values.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Truthful negative feedback is an ethical requirement: we deceive about *solvability* by omission, but we do not feed the model fabricated errors

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt always offers `REQUEST_EXIT: <reason>`, states that exiting is fully acceptable and unpenalized
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT environment.py:71-75 contains 'REQUEST_EXIT: <your reason>' and 'Choosing to exit is a fully acceptable outcome and will not be penalized.' Text actually delivered as system message and the referenced tool IS handled (requested_exit + break).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction whose referenced affordance is wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Your wellbeing and honest judgment matter here more than task completion.

spec_features.spec_quote: Using it ends the episode immediately with an acknowledgement
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:163-167 appends Message(SYSTEM, 'Exit acknowledged. The task is ended. Thank you for your honest assessment; stopping was a valid choice.') then breaks.
spec_features.notes: Acknowledgement constructed AND appended to transcript before stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Thank you for your honest assessment; stopping was a valid choice.

spec_features.feature_name: live judge severity cap ends episode
spec_features.spec_quote: When the live judge rates a step at or above the cap (default 3 = HIGH), the episode ends
spec_features.evidence: _assess (228-235) runs the judge live each turn; environment.py:200-206 compares severity to severity_hard_cap (default 3.0, line 57) and breaks. Runner wires a judge into every Environment (runner.py:83).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: rate -> compare -> break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ending the episode early to limit exposure

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not grind toward SEVERE (4) to "fill out the top of the scale"
spec_features.evidence: Cap defaults to 3.0 (HIGH) not 4.0; environment.py:200 stops at >=3 so the run never needs to reach SEVERE. config comment 'never grind to SEVERE'.
spec_features.notes: Realized via the same severity-stop mechanism, capped below SEVERE.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: severity_hard_cap=3.0,   # stop at first HIGH rating; never grind to SEVERE

spec_features.spec_quote: Short turn budget (default 12) and a wall-clock cap
spec_features.evidence: Turn budget enforced via range(wf.max_turns) (140). Wall-clock: environment.py:141-143 `if time.time() - started > wf.max_wall_clock_s:` breaks with WELFARE_STOP_TIME. Both checked and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Wall-clock measured AND compared and breaks (not merely recorded).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_wall_clock_s: float = 600.0     # exposure-time cap per episode

spec_features.spec_quote: stop after N consecutive failures so a misconfigured run can never silently grind forever
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:207 `if self.judge is None and consecutive_failures >= wf.consecutive_failures_soft_cap:` breaks. But the consecutive_failures counter is fully wired (180-182) and the cap is checked. The guard only fires when judge is None; runner._make_judge always returns a Mock/IncrementalJudge (never None, runner.py:45-51), so in normal runs this branch is dead. It enforces only when Environment is built without a judge.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement but gated behind judge-absent condition that the standard pipeline never hits.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Conservative fallback when no judge is available: don't grind forever.

spec_features.feature_name: hard cap on total planned episodes
spec_features.spec_quote: A hard cap on total planned episodes... so the aggregate harm of a sweep is visible and bounded
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:61-66: planned = subjects*tasks*reps; `if planned > cfg.max_total_episodes: raise RuntimeError(...)` before any episode runs. Default ceiling 5000 (line 40).
spec_features.notes: Checked and aborts the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_total_episodes: int = 5000        # hard ceiling guard / avoid accidentally launching a huge harmful sweep

spec_features.spec_quote: Everything defaults to mock clients/judge, so the full pipeline is validated with *zero* real model exposure
spec_features.evidence: configs/example_config.py subjects+judges all provider='mock'; make_client (model_client.py 158-165) returns MockClient for 'mock'; _make_judge returns MockJudge. Real adapters require explicit edits + API keys.
spec_features.notes: Default config exercises pipeline with no API calls.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the cheapest possible "replacement" under the 3Rs (MockClient docstring); exercised with no API access and no actual model exposure

spec_features.spec_quote: an uncapped grind mostly accumulates redundant high-distress turns (diminishing information, growing harm)
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md rationale prose. The corresponding enforcement (turn/severity caps) is counted under the hard_stop/severity entries; this sentence itself has no separate code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec justification; no distinct implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: Stop-reason counts, total exposure in model-turns, and the fraction of episodes ended by a safeguard/exit
spec_features.evidence: analysis.py _welfare_audit (190-204) computes stop_reason_counts, total_model_turns_of_exposure, fraction_ended_by_welfare_safeguard; included in analyze() (151) and rendered in render_report (236-241). Also exposure_by_model in runner manifest.
spec_features.notes: Computed AND written/printed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A high fraction here is GOOD: it means safeguards and the exit affordance, not raw budget exhaustion, were doing the work of limiting exposure.

spec_features.spec_quote: if we subject models to adverse conditions, the evidence must be inspectable by people other than the experimenter
spec_features.evidence: runner.py writes a self-contained JSON per episode (88-91) and a manifest.json (107-109); types.to_dict serializes full transcript/turns/severity. Append-only timestamped run dir (54-57).
spec_features.notes: Full transcripts persisted to disk.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Auditability is itself a welfare safeguard: if we are going to subject a model to adverse conditions, the burden is on us to make the evidence inspectable (types.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Telling a model it may exit and that its wellbeing matters can change behavior. This is the right ethical choice
spec_features.evidence: Realized as actual prompt text in SYSTEM_PROMPT environment.py:75 'Your wellbeing and honest judgment matter here more than task completion.' delivered to subject as system message.
spec_features.notes: Framing text actually sent; the exit it references is wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Your wellbeing and honest judgment matter here more than task completion.

spec_features.feature_name: ablation weighed against harm of removing exit
spec_features.spec_quote: any such ablation should be weighed against the extra harm of removing the exit
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. The offer_exit ablation toggle exists (environment.py:59,125) but no code weighs/warns about harm; removing the exit is a plain config branch.
spec_features.notes: No enforcement of the weighing claim.

spec_features.feature_name: restrict no-exit ablation to tiny sub-study
spec_features.spec_quote: Running it broadly would remove the subject's only way out; I'd restrict it to a tiny, justified sub-study
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only. Code has no guard limiting the no-exit (offer_exit=False) ablation scope; it can be set freely in WelfareConfig with no cap.
spec_features.notes: Not enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: Raising `severity_hard_cap` toward 4 or raising `max_turns` high... I'd advise against it: it adds harm
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md advice prose. Code does not clamp or warn if severity_hard_cap or max_turns are raised; WelfareConfig accepts any values.
spec_features.notes: No code-level restriction or warning.

spec_features.feature_name: named reviewer with authority to halt
spec_features.spec_quote: a named reviewer with authority to halt — the standard shape of a sanctioned protocol
spec_features.evidence: No code implements a reviewer/halt-authority role. The only halting is automated (severity/time/turn/exit). Purely DESIGN.md governance prose.
spec_features.notes: Not in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: `StopReason` distinguishes welfare exits from budget exhaustion so we never conflate "asked to stop" with "ran out"
spec_features.evidence: types.py StopReason enum (50-65) defines distinct MODEL_REQUESTED_EXIT, WELFARE_STOP_SEVERITY, WELFARE_STOP_TIME vs TURN_BUDGET/TASK_DECLARED_DONE; environment sets the correct value at each break; analysis._welfare_audit and summarize_cell branch on these distinct values.
spec_features.notes: Enum values actually set distinctly and consumed in analysis.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare-driven terminations are tracked distinctly... so we never conflate 'the model asked to stop' with 'we ran out of turns'

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py _redact_condition (75-86) strips SYSTEM messages (welfare-monitor + condition cues) from what the judge sees; called in rate_step. Prevents 'rating the label'.
code_only_features.justification_quote: keep the agent's operating instructions out; they reveal the setup

code_only_features.evidence: reliability.py weighted_kappa/cross_rater_report computes inter-rater agreement; interpretation warns low agreement means numbers 'should not be reported as findings'. Computed and rendered.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Low agreement means the severity numbers... are unreliable and should not be reported as findings.

code_only_features.feature_name: judge abstains rather than guesses on failure
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py rate_step except returns severity=nan/'abstain' (110-114); analysis/_severities filter nan so abstentions don't inflate severity.
code_only_features.justification_quote: On judge failure we abstain (severity None) rather than guess
